title: Finite-order Sobolev embedding for compact bundle sections
statement: All vector spaces are over $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field]. Let $N$ be a compact oriented smooth manifold without boundary of dimension $m\geq1$, with a smooth Riemannian metric and its positive volume form. For a smooth finite-rank real metric bundle $B$, let $L^2(B)$ be measurable square-integrable sections modulo almost-everywhere equality. For an integer $j\geq0$, let $H^j(B)$ be the subspace of $L^2(B)$ whose local coefficients in smooth coordinate charts and bundle frames have distributional derivatives through order $j$ locally in $L^2$. Fix Sobolev norms $\|\cdot\|_{H^j}$ obtained by a finite smooth coordinate trivializing cover and a subordinate smooth partition of unity, taking the square root of the sum of squared Euclidean $L^2$ norms of all derivatives through order $j$ of the localized sections. Here $H^0(B)=L^2(B)$, with its usual integrated norm $\|\cdot\|_{L^2}$. Distributional derivatives are taken by duality against compactly supported smooth test functions in each chart. Let $B$ be such a bundle and let $t,r\geq0$ be integers with $t>r+m/2$. Every $v\in H^t(B)$ has a unique $C^r$ section $v_r$ of $B$ whose almost-everywhere equivalence class is $v$. The statement concerns the representative of the given $L^2$ class, not only an abstract embedding into a space of functions.

source.place: WANTED locally; Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, June 21, 2012, VI §2, Sobolev lemma (2.1), printed p.289 (PDF page 289), including the preceding weak-derivative definition of the Sobolev spaces; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf

proof.text: Use the finite coordinate cover trivializing $B$ in the statement. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-subordinate-partition] with $M=S=N$ to obtain smooth $\chi_i\geq0$ with $\sum_i\chi_i=1$ and closed support contained in the corresponding chart $U_i$. Its hypotheses hold: $N$ is a compact Hausdorff smooth manifold, hence sigma-compact, and $S=N$ is closed. Each $K_i=\operatorname{supp}\chi_i$ is compact, since it is closed in $N$. Thus its image in the chart is a compact subset of the open coordinate image.

source.place: VI §2 (2.1), WANTED locally; agent-written Fourier/localization proof of the stated Sobolev lemma, with analytic inputs isolated as cited nodes. Demailly states the embedding without its Fourier proof; see report.md.

proof.text: For each frame component $f$ of $v$ on $U_i$, put $w=(\chi_i f)\circ x_i^{-1}$ on the coordinate image and zero outside it. It has weak derivatives in $L^2(\mathbf R^m)$ through order $t$. Indeed the test-function definition gives $\partial_j(\chi f)=(\partial_j\chi)f+\chi\partial_j f$: test against $\psi$, and use the defining identity for $\partial_j f$ with test $\chi\psi$. Inducting gives $\partial^\alpha(\chi f)=\sum_{\beta\leq\alpha}\binom\alpha\beta(\partial^{\alpha-\beta}\chi)\partial^\beta f$. Every summand is supported in the compact chart image of $K_i$, has bounded smooth multiplier, and is $L^2$ there by the local weak-derivative hypothesis. For zero extension the same calculation works against every global compactly supported test: each product $(\partial^\gamma\chi)\psi$ is itself compactly supported inside the chart, so every use of the defining weak identity is legitimate and introduces no boundary term. No change-of-coordinates regularity theorem is being assumed: the hypothesis already gives the weak derivatives in this very chart. Regard the real $w$ as complex-valued with zero imaginary part.

proof.text: For each such $w$, [lem-sfb-weak-sobolev-fourier-moments] applies with the given $m,t,r$, since $t>r+m/2$. It gives every integrable Fourier moment through order $r$. Apply [lem-sfb-fourier-moment-representative] to that same $L^2$ class and its Plancherel Fourier transform. Its inverse integral is $C^r$ and equals $w$ almost everywhere. Taking the real part gives a real $C^r$ function $g$ equal to $w$ almost everywhere. Outside the compact chart image of $K_i$, $w=0$ almost everywhere, and [lem-sfb-continuous-ae-pointwise], applied on its open complement to the complexification of $g$ and zero, gives $g=0$ pointwise there.

source.place: VI §2 (2.1), WANTED locally; agent-written Fourier/localization proof of the stated Sobolev lemma, with analytic inputs isolated as cited nodes. Demailly states the embedding without its Fourier proof; see report.md.

proof.text: Transfer these finitely many real functions back to their frame and chart to obtain a $C^r$ section $s_i$ on $U_i$, zero outside $K_i$. Extending $s_i$ by zero to $N$ is $C^r$: near every point of $N\setminus U_i$ there is a neighborhood disjoint from the closed set $K_i$, on which the extension is zero. Its almost-everywhere class is $\chi_i v$. Lebesgue-null sets in coordinates and volume-null sets coincide, since the volume form has a smooth strictly positive density $\rho$: $\int_E\rho=0$ implies that each $E\cap\{\rho\geq1/n\}$ is Lebesgue-null, and their union is $E$; the converse follows by integration over a null set. Consequently the finite sum $v_r=\sum_i s_i$ is $C^r$ and represents $(\sum_i\chi_i)v=v$. If $a,b$ are two such representatives, their continuous frame coefficients agree almost everywhere in every chart. Apply [lem-sfb-continuous-ae-pointwise] componentwise, using complexifications of these real coefficients, to obtain equality at every point. Hence $a=b$. This also handles the zero-rank bundle and the empty manifold.
